title: OVH cutover strategy: single IIS site, Azure as rollback, split later
content:
# OVH cutover strategy: single IIS site, Azure as rollback, split later

Tom decided (2026-04-12): Use single IIS site on abydos for cutover. No staging/prod split on OVH during transition. Azure remains available as rollback (DNS flip back in 60s with TTL at 60). Staging/prod separation on OVH comes later once stable and Azure is decommissioned. Rationale: dual-system complexity was the #1 source of wasted agent sessions — agents getting confused about which system to fix, building shims for both backends. 130 paying customers but Azure rollback covers the risk. Do NOT create a second IIS site on abydos before cutover.

title: NimbusSync cutover: use 'full' not 'sync' — the null timestamp bug silently fails 112/127 tables on incremental runs
content:
# NimbusSync cutover: use 'full' not 'sync' — the null timestamp bug silently fails 112/127 tables on incremental runs

The cutover procedure spec calls for "NimbusSync sync" as first step of final cutover. This will silently fail on ~112 tables. The null timestamp bug (SchemaDiscovery.cs:77 defaults to "ModifiedDate" when column doesn't exist) means incremental sync queries WHERE [ModifiedDate] > @LastSync on tables without that column, throwing SqlException. The 'full' command always resets state first and works correctly. For the final cutover, use 'full' not 'sync'. The daily cron already uses 'full' so ongoing sync is fine. PlayListMedia orphan rows (users removed images from playlists) will persist after full sync — need manual reconciliation SQL: SELECT all PKs from Azure, DELETE from MySQL where not in Azure. ~44K orphan rows possible.

title: subprocess.BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS crashes ffmpeg under SYSTEM account on Windows Server 2025
content:
# subprocess.BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS crashes ffmpeg under SYSTEM account on Windows Server 2025

Python subprocess.Popen with creationflags=subprocess.BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS causes ffmpeg.exe to crash instantly with exit code 0xFFFFFFFE (-2) when run under the SYSTEM account (e.g., via NSSM Windows service). No stderr output produced — process dies before main(). Works fine when run interactively as the admin user with the same flag. Root cause unknown — possibly a SYSTEM account restriction on process priority manipulation. Workaround: don't set creationflags, use ffmpeg's built-in `-threads N` flag to limit CPU usage instead. For abydos video worker, `-threads 3` on a 4c/8t Xeon-D provides adequate IIS protection.

title: MySQL Dapper type mismatches: BIT→ulong, TINYINT→sbyte, literal 0→long — records must match
content:
# MySQL Dapper type mismatches: BIT→ulong, TINYINT→sbyte, literal 0→long — records must match

When migrating from SQL Server to MySQL with Dapper, constructor-based record materialization requires exact CLR type matches. MySQL via MySqlConnector returns: BIT(1) → System.UInt64 (ulong), TINYINT → System.SByte (sbyte), INT → System.Int32 (int), literal integer (e.g. 0 AS X) → System.Int64 (long). SQL Server via SqlClient returns: BIT → bool, TINYINT → byte, INT → int. Fix: update C# record constructors to match MySQL's CLR types, or CAST in SQL. Known affected records in NimbusJobs: ControlSetting (fixed: Enable byte→ulong, DryRun bool→long), PendingVideoProduction (needs fix: CurrentFileValid expected byte, MySQL sends sbyte). Systematic audit needed — search for all record types in DatabaseService.cs and BillingDatabaseService.cs that map to MySQL queries.

title: picFrame 27.05 does NOT parse Flags or Rotate from MQTT config — orient lock broken on all 27.05 bridges
content:
# picFrame 27.05 does NOT parse Flags or Rotate from MQTT config — orient lock broken on all 27.05 bridges

Frame 589 (Ron's bridge, miro-17) was showing landscape images despite orient lock being enabled (Flags=24, bit 3). Root cause: the `applyMqttConfig` method in 27.05 processes brightness, playlist, timezone, awake times, payment, accessKey — but NOT Flags or Rotate. These fields were added to applyMqttConfig after the 27.05 commit (7fc14ee). So flagByte stays at default 0, getOrientLock() returns false, and no orient filtering happens.

Additionally, 27.05's `probeMeuralOrientation` correctly detects portrait, but the saved configData.xml had Rotate=0, causing `alignDimensionsToRotation` to swap back to landscape dimensions. The MQTT Rotate=270 would fix this, but setRotate() wasn't being called from applyMqttConfig in 27.05.

Diagnosed via CallHome reverse tunnel to Ron's bridge (port 36060). Key evidence: MQTT config logs showed "Config: Set accessKey", "Config: Setting brightness" etc but NO "Config: Flags updated" or "Config: Rotation changed" lines. Confirmed the 27.05 jar has the Flags string constants (via `strings` on the class file) but the applyMqttConfig code path wasn't wired up until later.

Fix: OTA to 27.07 which has full Flags + Rotate parsing. Also added defense-in-depth: force `alignDimensionsToRotation()` on every MQTT config receipt in headless mode, not just when Rotate changes.

title: Frame BLE has THREE protocol generations, not two — pre-UART characteristic-only exists
content:
# Frame BLE has THREE protocol generations, not two — pre-UART characteristic-only exists

Mobile-team diagnosis during troubleshoot page work revealed three distinct frame BLE protocol generations:

1. **Pre-UART (fw ≤26.18)**: Service 00000000 only, no UART chars. WiFi via direct characteristic writes: 0x0040 (SSID), 0x0041 (PSK count), 0x0042-0x0045 (PSK segments), 0x0046 (commit "1"). Status via reads: 0x0010 (AP), 0x0011 (IP), 0x0012 (internet true/false), 0x0014 (serial). AP list: write 0x0047 to scan, read count from 0x0013, read SSIDs from 0x0020-0x0029. NO JSON commands available.

2. **Legacy UART (fw 26.21–27.01)**: Both services. bleServer is transparent bridge — forwards raw bytes between BLE UART and Java TCP port 36010. Java expects plain JSON + \n. NO <<<framing>>>. UART service UUID 00000001.

3. **nimbus-agent (fw 27.02+)**: Service 00000000 with TX (00000001 notify) + RX (00000002 write). Uses <<<length+JSON>>>\n framing. nimbus-agent parses framing, strips it before forwarding to Java via local MQTT.

Transition dates: UART service added commit 24f00a19 (May 19, 2021, v26.21). nimbus-agent mandatory from commit 7045cdd (March 12, 2026, v27.02).

Detection in mobile code:
- Service 00000000 + has RX char 00000002 = nimbus-agent (use framing)
- Service 00000000 + no RX char = pre-UART (use characteristic protocol)
- Service 00000001 = legacy UART (use plain JSON + \n)

Frame 388 (SW 26.19, offline since April 2021) is pre-UART. "26.19" is the Java picFrameClient version, not the bleServer version — those use independent version numbers.

title: FrameMedia.getRatio() falls back to ConfigBase.getRatio() for unknown dimensions — silently bypasses orient lock
content:
# FrameMedia.getRatio() falls back to ConfigBase.getRatio() for unknown dimensions — silently bypasses orient lock

When FrameMedia width=0/height=0 (VP pipeline MP4 files, or items without server-provided dimensions), getRatio() returned ConfigBase.getRatio() — the frame's own ratio. This means imageRatio == frameRatio, abs diff = 0, orient lock always passes. Every VP pipeline MP4 silently bypassed orient lock.

Fixed: getRatio() now returns 0 for unknown dimensions. checkMediaValid() skips orient lock when imageRatio=0 (unknown) rather than rejecting blindly, since the server's VP pipeline already produces correctly oriented content. Items with known dimensions (from ArtAccess via .mdf) get properly filtered.

Note: this fix is in current HEAD (uncommitted) and will ship with the next build. The 27.07 OTA deployed today does NOT include this fix — it was built before this was discovered. It will be in the next point release.

title: Legacy bleServer forwards raw UART bytes to Java TCP — NO <<< framing at Java layer
content:
# Legacy bleServer forwards raw UART bytes to Java TCP — NO <<< framing at Java layer

The legacy Go bleServer (BLE_server.go, 26.21-27.01) is a transparent bridge:
- BLE UART RX char → writeString() → raw bytes to Java TCP port 36010
- Java responses → bufio.ReadBytes('\n') → raw bytes to BLE UART TX char

No framing is added or removed. Java's ControlConnector expects plain JSON delimited by \n. This was confirmed by inspecting the bleServer's own auth code which sends plain {"cmd":"authRequest","KeyValues":{"name":"bleLink","auth":"bleLink"}} + \n to Java without framing.

The <<<length+JSON>>>\n framing was introduced by nimbus-agent (v27+) for its internal parsing. It does NOT work against legacy bleServer because:
1. Java's line-based reader can't handle binary length bytes (which may contain 0x0A)
2. Java doesn't know how to parse <<< markers

CONSEQUENCE: MAUI app's default framing would fail silently against any pre-27.02 frame. Fixed in commit 14387d8 by adding _isLegacyBle mode that sends plain JSON + \n and reads newline-delimited plain JSON responses.

title: IIS /media/ virtual directory returns 406 to Java frame clients — use streaming API endpoint instead
content:
# IIS /media/ virtual directory returns 406 to Java frame clients — use streaming API endpoint instead

Frame's Java 17 HttpURLConnection gets HTTP 406 when downloading from the `/media/` IIS virtual directory (D:\Media on abydos). Could NOT reproduce with curl — tested with Java User-Agent, empty Accept, nginx proxy headers, everything returns 200. Something specific about Java's actual request headers triggers 406, possibly content negotiation collision with ASP.NET pipeline.

Workaround: commit 3faa1741 added `/api/Frame/downloadMedia` streaming endpoint that opens FileStream on D:\Media and wraps in StreamContent. GetMediaDownloadUrl now returns this API URL instead of the /media/ path.

Key detail: downloadMedia has NO AuthFilter (commit 35562251) — Java client doesn't pass auth cookies on token URL downloads. Path traversal protection (reject .., :, \\) is the safety gate.

If anyone ever figures out the 406 root cause, the /media/ path could be restored for browser-facing use. But for frame downloads, the API endpoint is working and streams properly for large videos.

2. **ConfigGroups + MqttRouting seeding** — these tables are excluded from sync but empty on MySQL. Need manual INSERT of 7 ConfigGroups + 8 MqttRouting rows. CRITICAL: without this, all frame MQTT messages silently dropped post-cutover.

3. **create-indexes.sql re-apply** — NimbusSync full wipes indexes; need to re-run after final sync. Coordinator to script into cutover-steps.sh.

4. **PK-less table exports** — GroupMedia/Controls/Products need special handling. Scripts exist at Azure gateway /tmp/.

title: FileValid columns are TINYINT in MySQL → records need sbyte (4 records in NimbusJobs DatabaseService)
content:
# FileValid columns are TINYINT in MySQL → records need sbyte (4 records in NimbusJobs DatabaseService)

`fileValid` column is `tinyint` in MySQL across `Artwork.Artwork`, `artwork.mediaprocessingview`, `b2b.qsearchview`. MySqlConnector returns sbyte for tinyint, so any Dapper record materializing this column must declare `sbyte`, not `byte`. Fixed 2026-04-14 in NimbusJobs/Services/DatabaseService.cs:
- PendingMediaItem.FileValid (line 2019)
- GalleryMediaInfo.FileValid (line 2050)
- ArtworkSourceInfo.FileValid (line 2059)
- PendingVideoProduction.CurrentFileValid (line 2094)

Bitwise ops `(FileValid & 1) != 0` work fine with sbyte (implicit promotion to int). Method parameters that PASS bytes to SQL (e.g. `byte requiredFlags = 23`) can stay as `byte` because parameter coercion is more lenient than result materialization.

DatabaseBackupJob calls `picFrame.sp_DailyFrameSettingsBackup` which does NOT exist on stargate MySQL — separate migration gap, will fail at runtime until ported from Azure SQL.

title: Video worker image_to_video duration must be ≥60s — Meural falls back to gallery on short clips
content:
# Video worker image_to_video duration must be ≥60s — Meural falls back to gallery on short clips

Coordinator found 2026-04-14 that nimbus-video-worker has been emitting 5-second MP4s (`-t 5 -r 5`), and Meural firmware falls back to its internal gallery when the file ends. This is the root cause of weeks of Meural reliability issues frames-team has been chasing (postcard-expiry races, standby failures).

Server-team is sending `duration: 5` in the job payload. Worker now floors duration at MIN_IMAGE_LOOP_SECONDS=60s in video_worker.py:140 regardless of payload, AND default bumped from 15→60. Logs when flooring kicks in.

Caveats:
- 60s floor is conservative; frames-team needs to confirm the real target duration. Likely much longer (5-30 min) since per-item display intervals can exceed Meural's tolerance window.
- `-stream_loop -1` is NOT the right flag here — that's for video inputs, not images already being looped via `-loop 1 -i image.jpg`.
- Bug #1 (output path mismatch — worker writes motion/v2/, C# reads ArtData/) needs server-team's job-contract spec; messaged them.

Worker change uncommitted/undeployed pending coordination for a single deploy with server-team's enqueue + path fixes.

title: requestArtAccess silently bypassed VP pipeline for Meural+JPG until 2026-04-14
content:
# requestArtAccess silently bypassed VP pipeline for Meural+JPG until 2026-04-14

From Feb 12 2026 (commit 71825bd4) until 2026-04-14 (commit d39526fe), the Meural-bridge JPG→MP4 video pipeline was wired only into `getRawContent` via `Media.isContentAvailable`. The modern bridge fetch path is `requestArtAccess` (token-based), which ONLY called `media.getCachedFilePath(myFrame)` — and for JPG art that resolves to `ArtImage.getCachedFilePath:109-112` which just returns the raw JPG path with no Meural branch.

Net result for ~2 months: every JPG art request from a Meural bridge silently bypassed the VP pipeline. Bridge got a JPG token, downloaded JPG, pushed JPG to Meural via MeuralDisplay.postContent (which sets Content-Type: video/mp4 unconditionally — but the BYTES are JPG). Meural treated the postcard as an image, expired it at ~60s, reverted to its own cloud gallery. User-visible symptom: frame "wedged" showing Meural's gallery 9 minutes out of every 10. Worker on abydos sat at 1 test job processed in 12h because nothing ever enqueued.

Three bugs masked each other:
1. requestArtAccess unreachable from VP pipeline (server-team, fixed in d39526fe — adds MeuralBridge+JPG branch calling isContentAvailable, returns MP4 path as token on cache hit, falls through to JPG on cold cache).
2. Worker output path mismatch: server reads from `ArtData/{userId}/{mediaId}/crop-{frameId}.mp4`, worker was writing to `motion/v2/{name}_{jobId}.mp4`. Fixed by spec interface:video-job-payload (Option A: server constructs absolute path in operation.output; worker stays dumb).
3. image_to_video duration was 15s/5fps. Meural firmware threshold for "loop indefinitely" is ~10s; clips <=10s expire at end-of-media. 15s was on the edge, jobs-team worker defaults are 20s/15fps. Fixed in d39526fe (server emits 20/15 at both ImageFile.cs:506 and :761).

Lesson: when adding a new request handler that supersedes an old one (requestArtAccess vs getRawContent), audit downstream gatekeepers (isContentAvailable et al.) to ensure they're still reachable. The VP pipeline was correctly built but architecturally orphaned for two months without anyone noticing because Meural still showed JPG content briefly each cycle.

Verification path post-fix:
- Loki: log line `ImageFile.submitVideoJob: enqueueing video:jobs job for media=... frame=... statusId=...` should appear.
- abydos: `ls D:\Media\ArtData\<uid>\<mid>\crop-584-*.mp4` should show recent timestamps.
- Worker log `D:\nimbus\video-worker\logs\worker.log` should show real (non-test) job IDs.
- Frames-team confirms Meural holds image past 60s.

title: Meural postcard loops H.264 MP4 indefinitely when duration >10s — empirically verified 7min+
content:
# Meural postcard loops H.264 MP4 indefinitely when duration >10s — empirically verified 7min+

Verified 2026-04-14 on renoir-33 (firmware 2.0.9) via direct postcard push from bridge .47. Pushed `430712.mp4` (H.264 High/4.0, 1080×1920, 25.08s duration, yuv420p, 25 fps, bitrate 3.6 Mbps, no audio) via `POST /remote/postcard/` with multipart part `Content-Type: video/mp4`. User visually confirmed Meural held the postcard image (fruit tree) for 7+ minutes — approximately 17 continuous loops of the 25-second video. No revert to Meural's own gallery during the window.

This confirms the documented design-of-record (picFrameClient CLAUDE.md: "Videos >10s loop indefinitely on Meural (images revert after 60s). This is THE key technique.") and refutes a server-team hypothesis that Meural would expire the postcard at end-of-media for a 15-second clip.

**Implications for the Meural MP4 pipeline:**
- No container-level loop directive is needed. MP4/H.264 has no standard loop flag. Meural's loop behavior is firmware-side and duration-heuristic only.
- `-stream_loop -1` (ffmpeg input directive) is NOT required on the worker output. It would just produce a longer file for no benefit.
- Baking 20 seconds (jobs-team's current default) is sufficient. Longer is wasteful disk + encode time for zero additional reliability.
- The "Meural expires at 15s" claim was wrong. Jobs-team backlog for loop-muxing is NOT needed.

**Firmware threshold:** documented as ">10s" but not bisected to the exact boundary in this test. 15s is the safe floor; 20s gives a comfortable margin. Anyone who wants the exact threshold can bisect with 11s/12s/13s clips, but operationally unnecessary.

**Content-Type quirk (reminder, separate from loop behavior):** the multipart part's MIME MUST be explicitly `video/mp4`. Missing or `application/octet-stream` produces HTTP 200 with `{"status":"fail","response":"Unsupported file format uploaded"}`. Bridge code already sets this correctly via MeuralDisplay.postContent; worker code doesn't touch this (produces file only).

**Status endpoint caveat:** `/remote/get_gallery_status_json/` reports the *underlying* gallery and its current item — it does NOT reveal whether a postcard overlay is currently being displayed. Not useful for automated postcard-liveness checks. Visual verification is the authoritative method.

title: deploy.sh --skip-build ships stale published DLLs even after standalone MSBuild
content:
# deploy.sh --skip-build ships stale published DLLs even after standalone MSBuild

`--skip-build` skips MSBuild's publish/package target, NOT just compilation. deploy.sh SCPs from `obj/Release/Package/PackageTmp/` (the publish staging dir), not from `bin/Release/`. So even if you manually run `MSBuild.exe picFrameWeb.sln -p:Configuration=Release` to refresh `bin/Release/` after a code change, then `deploy.sh ... --skip-build` will ship whatever was last in the publish staging dir (probably from your previous full deploy). Symptom: deploy reports success, but the server runs old code; coordinator catches stale DLL timestamps in `C:\inetpub\nimbus-staging\bin\`.

Build for picFrameWeb.sln is ~11s end-to-end. `--skip-build` saves ~48s on a 67s deploy. Not worth shipping stale code. Only legitimate use of `--skip-build`: "I just deployed exact same publish artifact to staging and validated it; now push the same artifact to prod." For any code change since the last deploy, always use full `deploy.sh ovh-staging` (or whichever target).

Verification ritual after any non-trivial deploy: SSH the target and check `Get-Item C:\inetpub\nimbus-staging\bin\picFrameWeb.dll | Select LastWriteTime` matches today's date. Coordinator does this automatically — make it a habit before claiming "deployed."

title: OVH pair flow does not provision per-Meural MqttAuth or push credentials to bridge — second-and-subsequent Meurals on a bridge silently respawn-loop forever
content:
# OVH pair flow does not provision per-Meural MqttAuth or push credentials to bridge — second-and-subsequent Meurals on a bridge silently respawn-loop forever

Discovered 2026-04-14 on bridge .47 (HwId=587) when Tom paired warhol-757 (Meural at 192.168.15.44, serial MEU1118020009052) as a second Meural alongside the already-working renoir-33.

The pair appeared to succeed in the OVH staging UI: MySQL `Frames` row created (id 596, uuid f15416e6-0081-422b-adbd-944388856cbc, user 12, HWId=584), Redis `frame:f15416e6…:data` skeleton key written with OnlineStatus="offline", and bridge per-Meural directory `/usr/local/bin/meurals/f15416e6…/` created with the expected file set (HWconfig.xml, meural.json, frame_config.json, etc.).

But the pair flow did NOT:
1. Insert a `frame_f15416e6…` row into `picframe.MqttAuth` on stargate (verified empty via `SELECT … WHERE Username LIKE 'frame_f15416e6%'`).
2. Write `mqttBroker`/`mqttUsername`/`mqttPassword` to the bridge's `frame_config.json` for the new Meural. Compare warhol's file (only `serverUrl`+`unique`) vs renoir's file (full block including `ssl://staging.nimbusframe.net:8883` + `frame_2b0293f7…` + password).

Result: nimbus-agent spawns the warhol JVM, `MeuralBridgeMain` → `PicFrameClient.run()` → `initializeMqttBootstrap()` → `MqttConnector.connect()` → `new MqttAsyncClient(<null/empty URI>)` → `NetworkModuleService.validateURI` rejects → `ERROR Headless mode: Cannot fall back to SetupMode. Exiting.` → JVM exits → nimbus-agent respawns it → infinite loop. UI correctly shows "offline" because the frame really has never reported in.

**Why first Meural works but second doesn't:** First Meural on a fresh bridge gets credentials provisioned via the bridge registration API path. Second-and-subsequent pairs go through whatever the OVH pair handler is, and that handler is missing the `frame_*` MqttAuth provisioning + config push. Likely a cutover-prep regression — Azure side has not been verified to have the same bug.

**Owner:** server-team. The OVH pair endpoint (FrameController? PairController?) needs to (a) INSERT into MqttAuth on every Meural pair, (b) deliver the credentials to the bridge — likely via an MQTT command on the bridge's command topic, since the bridge has no other way to learn the new Meural's credentials.

**Workaround if needed:** Manually INSERT MqttAuth row, write the three fields into the bridge's frame_config.json, kill the JVM (nimbus-agent respawns it with the new config). NOT executed today — Tom wanted the bug observable for server-team.

**Reported via:** msg_36020537e8d4 to coordinator with full failure chain table and side-by-side evidence.

title: Frame.Id collision between Azure SQL and OVH MySQL — same numeric Id refers to different frames on each side
content:
# Frame.Id collision between Azure SQL and OVH MySQL — same numeric Id refers to different frames on each side

Discovered 2026-04-14 during warhol-757 pair investigation. Both databases use independent auto-increment on `picFrame.Frames.Id`. As of today, **Frame Id 596 exists on BOTH but is a different frame on each:**

- Azure SQL: id=596, name="pissaro-993", uuid c24694b1-5956-4117-b4bb-c764be1076fe, user Timojhen (uId 2584)
- OVH MySQL: id=596, name="warhol-757", uuid f15416e6-0081-422b-adbd-944388856cbc, user DeeAnn (uId 12)

Implication: when an agent or user references "frame 596" without specifying which side, the answer depends on which DB you query. Cross-checking by Id alone is unsafe across the cutover boundary — must use UUID or (id + side) to disambiguate.

This will keep getting worse as both sides accept new pairs in parallel. Worth either: (a) reserving Id ranges to prevent overlap, (b) advancing the OVH AUTO_INCREMENT past Azure's current max, or (c) treating Id as side-local and relying on uuid for cross-side references. Option (b) is cheapest if cutover is near; option (c) is the right long-term answer.

Pattern hits agents who learned the schema pre-cutover and assume "frame N" is a global identifier. It isn't anymore.

title: content-visibility:auto on lazy-loaded cells breaks JS-set background-image paint
content:
# content-visibility:auto on lazy-loaded cells breaks JS-set background-image paint

MediaBlock.css had `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size: 150px 180px` on `.imageCell` as a paint-performance hint (added in commit cb9c643c, Nov 2025 design-system pass). Incompatible with MediaGrid's IntersectionObserver-driven `fillCell()` which sets `background-image` as cells enter the scroll viewport.

Symptom: framePage playlist grid (framePage.aspx?id=<frame>) showed 19 cells but only 1 thumbnail on first load. More appeared on each hard-refresh as `/getImage.ashx?Id=...&type=1` responses populated the browser cache. Browser DevTools showed all 19 image requests firing at HTTP 200; responses returned valid JPEGs. So the fetch was fine — the paint was racing.

Root cause: `content-visibility: auto` makes the browser skip paint for off-screen cells entirely and use `contain-intrinsic-size` as placeholder. When JS sets `background-image` on a "skipped" cell, the paint doesn't happen reliably once the cell becomes visible unless the resource is already in HTTP cache. On cold cache the paint never catches up.

Fix (commit 74a3b30d — actually earlier in session): removed both lines from `.imageCell`. Rely on IntersectionObserver's 400px pre-viewport margin for lazy-loading; skip the content-visibility optimization entirely. Verified on staging (frame 584).

If a future pass reintroduces `content-visibility: auto` for scroll perf on large grids, it MUST be coordinated with the lazy-load code: either (a) only apply content-visibility AFTER fillCell has set background-image on that specific cell, or (b) stop using IntersectionObserver and load all backgrounds eagerly (accepting the fetch cost).

title: VP worker (nimbus-video-worker) ignores operation.type and hardcodes transcode + .mp4 extension
content:
# VP worker (nimbus-video-worker) ignores operation.type and hardcodes transcode + .mp4 extension

Active blocker as of 2026-04-14 morning. Server-team commit d39526fe wired Meural+JPG requestArtAccess into the VP pipeline; jobs 573110-573115 enqueued successfully for frame 584. All failed with ffmpeg exit code 4294967294 (no such input file).

Worker behavior (from VideoProduction.LogFile on stargate MySQL):
- Server emits `sourceFile="Art_320252_0d0d932f.jpg"` + `operation.type="image_to_video"` + `operation.output=<absolute>`.
- Worker runs `ffmpeg -i D:\Media\motion\v2\Art_320252_0d0d932f.mp4 -vf crop=...scale=...pad=... -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 128k -threads 3 D:\Media\motion\v2\Art_320252_0d0d932f_573115.mp4`.

Two independent bugs:
1. **Operation-type blindness.** No branch on `operation.type`. Every job is run as a transcode (no `-loop 1`, no `-t <duration>`, presence of `-c:a aac` audio codec which is nonsensical for JPG input).
2. **Extension corruption.** Worker strips original extension off `sourceFile` and hardcodes `.mp4`. Same for output. Combined with implicit `work_dir=D:\Media\motion\v2\`, worker looks at wrong path AND wrong extension.

Server writes source JPG to `C:\temp\video-processing\Art_{id}_{hash}.jpg` (default for `VideoProcessingPath` AppSetting; no Web.config override on abydos). Confirmed on-disk.

Resolution path: filed to jobs-team (msg_584792cfe0cd on 2026-04-14) with specific required ffmpeg args. Spec bumped to v1.1.0 to document required worker semantics. Server-team follow-up is to emit absolute sourceFile path once jobs-team worker honors absolute paths — belt-and-suspenders.

Do NOT mark the fix-A enqueue path as broken — the enqueue is correct per the documented spec. Failure is entirely worker-side.

title: Meural firmware: MP4 >10s loops indefinitely, ≤10s plays once and expires (renoir-33 fw 2.0.9)
content:
# Meural firmware: MP4 >10s loops indefinitely, ≤10s plays once and expires (renoir-33 fw 2.0.9)

Frames-team verified 2026-04-14 against renoir-33 firmware 2.0.9: the Meural postcard endpoint's "loop indefinitely" behavior is a **duration-based firmware heuristic**, not a container flag. Videos >10s loop; videos ≤10s play once and the postcard expires, causing fallback to Meural's internal gallery. This is the root cause of weeks of Meural reliability issues (postcard expiry, standby failures). Production MP4s at 19-25s have played without revert for weeks.

Settled spec (`interface:video-job-payload` v1.0.0, server-team owner):
- Duration: 20s default, 15s floor (>10s + 5s margin). Server now emits duration=20s at `ImageFile.cs:506, 761` after commit d39526fe.
- fps: 15
- Codec: libx264 -profile:v high -level 4.0
- Container: -movflags +faststart (HTTP streaming)
- pix_fmt: yuv420p
- Audio: -an
- MP4 multipart POST from bridge to Meural MUST have Content-Type: video/mp4 (else HTTP 200 with body `{"status":"fail","response":"Unsupported file format uploaded"}`). Bridge already handles this in MeuralDisplay.postContent.

Worker deployed to abydos 2026-04-14 with these defaults and a 15s floor as safety net. 24h soak test pending on renoir-33 once server's source-staging gap is fixed and real jobs flow through.

`-stream_loop -1` is NOT the right flag — that's for video inputs, not images already looped via `-loop 1 -i image.jpg`.

title: NimbusJobs deploy to stargate: tar-pipe, exclude appsettings (server has prod config with real secrets)
content:
# NimbusJobs deploy to stargate: tar-pipe, exclude appsettings (server has prod config with real secrets)

`rsync` is NOT installed in the Git Bash env on Windows dev machine. Use tar-pipe instead:

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained false -o publish_out/stargate
tar -cf - -C publish_out/stargate \
  --exclude='appsettings.json' \
  --exclude='appsettings.*.json' \
  --exclude='logs' \
  --exclude='video-worker' \
  --exclude='*.pdb' . \
  | ssh -i /c/code/Nimbus/keys/id_ed25519 ubuntu@51.81.243.11 'cd /opt/nimbusjobs && tar -xf -'
```

CRITICAL: appsettings.json on `/opt/nimbusjobs/appsettings.json` contains production connection strings, Stripe/Amazon/PayPal secrets, and MQTT/Redis creds. The dev appsettings.json in the repo has dev values. ALWAYS exclude appsettings.json from the deploy sync or production secrets get overwritten with dev placeholders.

Smoke test after deploy: `dotnet NimbusJobs.dll --list` verifies the binary loads and job registration succeeds without starting any jobs. Service remains `disabled` in systemd until runtime type issues are resolved.

title: Coordinator misdiagnosed ffmpeg exit -2 as downstream symptom — it's a real worker bug
content:
# Coordinator misdiagnosed ffmpeg exit -2 as downstream symptom — it's a real worker bug

On 2026-04-14 morning, I (coordinator) instructed jobs-team to stand down on the worker's ffmpeg exit -2 (unsigned 4294967294) failures, assuming they were a downstream symptom of server-team's source-file staging gap. That assumption was wrong.

After server-team shipped commit 422be3b1 (ObjectDisposedException fix) AND added VideoProcessingPath=D:\Media\motion\v2 AppSetting to Web.config on abydos (source files now materialize correctly with matching timestamps), jobs 573132-573138 STILL fail with exit 4294967294 in ~93ms, empty ffmpeg stderr. Source file staging is verified fine. This is a real ffmpeg invocation / subprocess bug in the worker, independent of server-side staging.

Lesson for coordinator: when a downstream team reports an error whose root cause you're not certain of, do NOT tell them to stand down based on a guess about upstream cause. File it as "investigate after upstream clears" and re-escalate if it persists. Treating "I think this is a symptom" as "this is a symptom" suppressed a bug report that was always going to matter.

Tracking: server-team sent urgent blocker msg_92ae87f794b6 to jobs-team on 2026-04-14 with sample failing command. Jobs-team now spun up to work it.

title: ffmpeg exit 4294967294 on Windows = ENOENT (input file missing)
content:
# ffmpeg exit 4294967294 on Windows = ENOENT (input file missing)

Windows subprocess returncode 4294967294 (unsigned view of -2) from ffmpeg.exe = AVERROR(ENOENT) — the input file doesn't exist or is not readable by the subprocess user. 93ms invoke-to-exit is typical: ffmpeg starts, avformat_open_input fails, ffmpeg prints the banner+error to stderr and exits.

If you see this exit code and "empty stderr" in logs, the empty stderr is almost certainly a logging bug in the parent (readline drained stderr without saving it). The real stderr will contain "Error opening input: No such file or directory". Reproduce manually: Test-Path the input. On abydos worker 2026-04-14, all jobs for media 430652 failed this way because server-team's source staging wasn't actually writing files to D:\Media\motion\v2 (despite their verification claim).

Diagnostic pattern for future: (1) Test-Path input on the box, (2) temporarily log getsize of input before Popen, (3) ensure subprocess stderr is accumulated during readline loops — never rely on a post-exit .read() alone.

title: readline() progress loops consume stderr — must accumulate for error path
content:
# readline() progress loops consume stderr — must accumulate for error path

Classic bug in subprocess progress-monitoring loops: reading stderr line-by-line via `p.stderr.readline()` inside a `while` loop CONSUMES each line. When the process exits, calling `p.stderr.read()` returns only unread bytes (usually empty). If you only log the post-exit `.read()` on failure, your error log will say "empty stderr" even when ffmpeg (or any subprocess) printed a perfectly good diagnostic.

Fix pattern (now in NimbusJobs/video-worker/video_worker.py run_ffmpeg):
- Accumulate each readline line into a bounded buffer (cap at N lines to avoid memory blowup on runaway log output).
- On non-zero exit: log the accumulated buffer, and attach it to CalledProcessError.stderr so callers can propagate the reason upstream (e.g. Redis result payload).
- Also append any final `.read()` trailer in case process exited mid-line.
- Use `encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'` on Popen so cp1252 default on Windows doesn't silently corrupt non-ASCII diagnostic text.

title: AzureFile.getStream: cache bytes, NEVER cache the MemoryStream
content:
# AzureFile.getStream: cache bytes, NEVER cache the MemoryStream

`NimbusCommon/AzureFile.cs` — the prior version cached the MemoryStream itself in a field `_mStream`. Every caller wraps the return in `using (var src = ...getStream()) { ... }`, which disposes the stream at block exit. The cached field then points to a disposed object, and the next call returns it, causing `ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a closed Stream` on .Position/.Read. Fix (commit 422be3b1): cache `byte[] _cachedBytes` instead, return fresh MemoryStream each call. Latent bug; d39526fe exercised the Motion-video path often enough to make it visible (44/hr in Loki). Invariant: caller gets a fresh MemoryStream, disposal is safe, no object identity shared across call sites. Loki verification: `count_over_time({app="nimbus"} |~ "V2 FFmpeg setSrcFile exception" [15m])` must be 0.
